observations.text: The task config at the target has an additional praxis object; task.py requires an exact five-key set, and baseline.prepare calls load_task before its qualification receipt and readiness checks.

The protocol file digest is 0eda1a046d4d9c456a3ee5a281cc183eaf188b0ff9db9fe0767bc5f6011dc803, matching the formal task. The #176 design and #177 integrity commits are ancestors of the target, and the formal task uses the #177 result as its diff base.
The shared identity validator requires all five Praxis values but compares only repository, branch, and commit; issue number and task path are presence-only checks.

The review validator checks an exact head, approved science/execution roles, nonempty reviewer/evidence values, and different reviewer labels. Authorization binds head, protocol hash, prepared manifest hash, and attempt budget, while accepting any nonempty user_instruction.

Preparation uses a zero-step guard and checks plant step count, time, and snapshot; qualification validates native plant_time_s is zero. The targeted qualification test-source scan found no real mj_step calls beyond a mocked function.

Capture checks for an existing permanent ledger, creates the ledger exclusively after fresh preflight, claims cases individually, continues performance failures, stops on safety or integrity failures, and suppresses cases dependent on a failed sentinel.
The baseline CLI's default task is rl_source_v1.json, so #178 must pass its capability-map task JSON explicitly.

inferences.text: With the target task JSON supplied, baseline.prepare will raise invalid task schema before it can return READY_AWAITING_START; this follows from the exact key-set check and call order and was not dynamically exercised because preparation is prohibited.
Issue number and task path exactness require the task's explicit manual capture-boundary check; they cannot be inferred from successful project-level identity validation.
The capture and offline verifier both enforce the sealed digest over raw rows, but they share the analyzer and digest-gate helper, leaving no second hash implementation.

conclusions.text: The execution review verdict is VETO because the formal task config is incompatible with the target's strict task loader. Resolve the task metadata/loader binding before starting #178; do not create authorization or invoke capture against this target.

The prior #176/#177 branch identities and result commits do not themselves block #178; their commit references and diff base are coherent. The generic CLI default must still be overridden with the capability-map task JSON.
The review task is complete: one JSON file was committed, parses successfully, and the worktree is clean.
